Which machine the app runs on, and with it what it may trade on. Its properties are the one table of what each

TechnicalReport.description:
Result produced by a TechnicalStrategy.

Hard failures reject the stock.
Soft failures reduce technical quality without rejecting the stock.
Observations describe optional technical signals.

TechnicalRule-Input.description: A condition and what passing or failing it does to the score. The name is a label: the condition alone decides.
TechnicalRule-Input.title: TechnicalRule

TechnicalRule-Output.description: A condition and what passing or failing it does to the score. The name is a label: the condition alone decides.

TechnicalScoring.description:
Each rule's effect applies once, however many conditions it holds: a failed block_on_fail rule rejects the stock
and costs block_failure_penalty, a failed reduce_score_on_fail rule costs failure_score_reduction, and a passed
increase_score_on_pass rule adds pass_score_increase. Passing a block_on_fail rule adds nothing.

TechnicalSettings-Input.description:
One owner's strategies and which one each workflow uses: the Buzz strategy for Buzz, the active one for every
other workflow. revision counts the owner's saves, so a save from an older read is refused instead of overwriting.
TechnicalSettings-Input.title: TechnicalSettings

TechnicalSettings-Output.description:
One owner's strategies and which one each workflow uses: the Buzz strategy for Buzz, the active one for every
other workflow. revision counts the owner's saves, so a save from an older read is refused instead of overwriting.
TechnicalSettings-Output.title: TechnicalSettings

indicator id such as ind_a never holds a parameter: changing ind_a's period changes every rule that reads ind_a,
and a rule that needs a different period reads another indicator.

TechnicalStrategy-Output.description:
The user's formulas over named indicators, scored together. strategy_id is a stable key and name a label. An
indicator id such as ind_a never holds a parameter: changing ind_a's period changes every rule that reads ind_a,
and a rule that needs a different period reads another indicator.
TechnicalStrategy-Output.title: TechnicalStrategy

TimeInForce.description: How long an accepted order keeps working (Taiwan exchange terms).
TimeInForce.title: TimeInForce

A person who signs in, and the owner of their own mock account, watchlist, records and strategies. It holds no

APIKeyCookie.name: stock_agent_session

info.description:
Runs the stock-agent workflows and reads what they recorded, on the same runtime as the CLI.

Users. Anyone may register (`POST /v1/auth/register`) while registration is open, and signs in with a username or an
email (`POST /v1/auth/sign-in`), which sets the HttpOnly session cookie `stock_agent_session`. Public: sign-in,
registration, the first-time setup, the built-in strategies and market data (`/v1/market`). Signed in: every other
read and write, each on the user's own runs, decisions, orders, watchlist, mock account and saved technical settings.
Administrator: the users (`/v1/admin/users`) and the settings files (`/v1/admin/settings*`). 401 means sign in: the
session is missing, expired or ended. 403 means signed in but not allowed, and never ends the session. Every write
sends the header `X-Requested-With: stock-agent`, and every write but sign-in, sign-out, registration and setup
repeats `"confirm": true` in its body.

Orders. Full Cycle, specific-stock analysis, valuation and market data never order. Buzz and Intraday send orders
through the same gates and trading journal as the CLI, and the API starts them only while the execution provider is
the mock broker (403 otherwise). No endpoint places, cancels or modifies an order by itself, and the API offers no
manual BUY.

Workflows run in the background, one at a time per user and a few at a time per server: a start answers 202 with the
run id, and GET /v1/runs/{run_id} reports the run's state and its record; another user's run id answers 404. Run the
server with one worker process.
info.title: TW-Stock-Alpha-Agent

get.description: Menu 7: the account now, its equity curve, and the account at the end of `as_of`. It never orders and records no run.
The latest saves and restores, newest first: when, which file, by whom, which revisions and which settings. No value.

schema.title: Response Get Settings Audit V1 Admin Audit Get

get.description:
Every settings file with its revision on disk and the one the server runs on, an edit on disk the server refused and
why, how many earlier settings still finish runs, and what applies only at a restart.

post.description:
The settings form's view of a text of appsetting.yaml: the text with each change written over its setting's value
in place, every other line, comment and key as it was; every setting the text then sets, by dotted path (null while
the text does not parse); and the JSON schema of what each setting accepts. Nothing is written: the page checks and
saves the text it answers like any text the administrator types.

422.description: A change the text cannot take (settings_edit_refused): the text does not parse, the path names no setting it sets, or the value is of another kind than the one there.

post.description:
The administrator's try again: loads the settings files as they are on disk now, an edit the server refused
before included, since a refusal can come from outside the files (a database that was down, a broker login that
failed). The server runs on them when they start, and the answer's `refused` is null; or it keeps its settings,
and `refused` says why.

get.description: The whole file as it is on disk, with its revision and the one the server runs on.

put.description:
Opens the app on the whole new text, writes it and runs on it at once, when the app starts with it, the file is
still at `revision` and the password is the administrator's own; or refuses with nothing written and the app as it
was. Runs that started earlier finish on the settings they started with.

403.description: A save or a restore without the password (password_required), or with a wrong one (password_refused).

409.description: The file changed after the revision the request carries; nothing saved.

422.description: The app would not start with it.

429.description: Too many wrong passwords from this address; Retry-After says when.

schema.title: Response List Settings Backups V1 Admin Settings  File  Backups Get

post.description: The backup's whole text against the file on disk, reviewed as a save would be. Nothing is written.
Puts the backup's whole text back through the same checks, password, startup, backup, audit and swap as a save.

403.description: A save or a restore without the password (password_required), or with a wrong one (password_refused).

409.description: The file changed after the revision the request carries; nothing saved.

422.description: The app would not start with it.

429.description: Too many wrong passwords from this address; Retry-After says when.

post.description:
The text against the file on disk: its diff, the settings it changes, those applying only at a restart, and its
problems at their line and column. Nothing is written.

get.description: Every user, oldest first. No administrator sees another user's data: this is the directory only.

schema.title: Response List Users V1 Admin Users Get

patch.description:
Changes a role, deactivates or reactivates a user, or sets a new password. A deactivation or a new password ends
every session of the user at once; their data stays, and a run of theirs already running finishes.

409.description: No active administrator would remain; nothing saved.

get.description: The signed-in user with their permissions, which the app reads to show the administration pages. 401 when signed out.
My settings: the AI models the site offers, its default, and the one the user's runs use. 401 when signed out.

put.description:
Chooses the AI model of the user's next runs, or null for the site's default. A run already running keeps its model.
A model the site stopped offering later leaves the choice saved, and the runs use the site's default meanwhile.

422.description: The site does not offer that model; nothing saved.

post.description: A new user with the role user: 403 while registration is closed, 409 for a taken username or email, 429 past the limit.

First use only: the administrator, who takes over the data of the single-user version. It needs the setup code the
server printed on its console at start (403 otherwise), so the first visitor of an exposed server cannot claim it.
409 once a user exists. The app then signs in like any user.
Sets the session cookie. 401 for a wrong name or password, one message for both; 429 past the attempt limits.
Ends this browser's session and clears its cookie. Signing out twice is fine.

get.description:
The owner's strategies and which one each workflow uses, with the revision a save must carry. The first read
copies every built-in strategy for the owner. A workflow already running keeps the strategy it started with. A
save that lands during the read answers 409: read again.

put.description:
Replaces the owner's settings as a whole, for the next workflow. Invalid settings save nothing and answer 422 with
one error per field under body.settings. Settings read before another save answer 409 and save nothing: read
them again, reapply the change, and save with the new revision.

get.description: The developer's strategies. A client copies one under its own strategy_id to start an owner's strategy from it.

post.description: One paid AI call: the AI explains the domain's numbers for one stock with its news. It adds no number.

get.description: The market reference: last closed session, the median P/E and the sources' warnings. The first load reads MOPS.

Menu 6: every stock valued at the target P/E, kept when at least `min_undervaluation` (a ratio) below its base
fair price. With `technical`, the survivors then go through the owner's active strategy, which loads their daily
history. No AI call.
Menu 5: the stocks' valuation facts, and their three scenarios at the target P/E. An unknown id is left out.
Every active entry: one per stock and watchlist type. A MANUAL entry never expires; TECHNICAL and BUZZ entries do.

schema.title: Response Get Watchlist V1 Watchlist Get

post.description:
Adds listed stocks to the MANUAL watchlist, as menu 4 does after an analysis. An unlisted ID adds nothing at all and
answers 422; an unavailable listing answers 503.
Takes stocks off the MANUAL watchlist only. A TECHNICAL or BUZZ entry of the same stock stays until it expires.
Answers each text message in a LINE webhook call. A call without LINE's signature over its body is refused.
